---
title: "A Windows path pasted as is breaks the string"
ref: STR-04
categories: [Strings]
impact: cryptique
extrait: '"C:\Users\me"'
attendu: "the path `C:\\Users\\me`"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
#| eval: false
path <- "C:\Users\me\data.csv"
```
:::

Run this block: R answers `Error: '\U' used without hex digits in character string`.

## Why

In an R string, the backslash starts an escape sequence: `\n` is a newline, `\t` a tab, and `\U` must be followed by the hexadecimal code of a Unicode character. `\Users` is not one, hence the error, raised before anything runs, while the code is being read.

The worst case is the one that does not fail: `"C:\temp\new"` is a valid string, which contains a tab and a newline. The file is simply never found.

## The fix

Write paths with forward slashes, which Windows accepts, or double the backslashes. Since R 4.0.0, a raw string `r"(...)"` keeps the text as is.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
"C:/Users/me/data.csv"
"C:\\Users\\me\\data.csv"
r"(C:\Users\me\data.csv)"
file.path("C:", "Users", "me", "data.csv")
```
:::
